title: Slot Pattern
description: Learn how to use the slot pattern to create flexible, composable components that accept arbitrary content at named injection points.

blocks.text: The slot pattern is a composition technique where a parent component defines named regions, or slots, that consumers can fill with arbitrary content. It is inspired by web components and Angular content projection, but in React it is typically implemented with props.children, named children, or render props. Slots let you build highly reusable layout components while giving downstream developers control over specific regions of the UI.

blocks.title: Why Slots Matter
blocks.text: Without slots, you either bake every possible variation into a prop explosion or force consumers to wrap your component in awkward wrapper elements. Slots give you the best of both worlds: a stable outer shell with customizable inner regions.

React's props.children gives you an unnamed default slot. To create named slots, you can pass multiple render props or use a composition object. Each slot receives the data it needs to render independently. The parent component orchestrates layout and context, while each slot focuses only on its own content.

terms.definition: The unnamed children prop that renders inside the main content area of a component.
A labeled content region, such as header, sidebar, or footer, passed via a dedicated prop or composition object.
The act of passing JSX from a parent into a child component so the child decides where to render it.
Data passed from the parent down into each slot's render function, enabling slots to access context or state.

blocks.text: A Card component is a classic example. It has a header, body, and footer. Instead of creating separate Header, Body, and Footer components and expecting users to nest them manually, you can define a single Card component that accepts named slot props. This keeps the JSX clean and prevents invalid nesting.

blocks.title: Card Component with Named Slots
blocks.content: A Card component that accepts header, body, and footer slots.

blocks.text: Use optional chaining and short-circuit evaluation when rendering slots. This prevents empty wrapper elements when a slot is not provided.

Sometimes a slot needs data from the parent component, such as loading state, error messages, or pagination controls. In those cases, the slot should be a function that receives the data as an argument. This is the render prop variant of the slot pattern. It gives the slot full control over how to use the data without tightly coupling the child to the parent's state shape.

blocks.title: DataList with Render Prop Slots
blocks.content: A list component that passes item data and loading state into slot render functions.

blocks.title: When to Use Render Prop Slots
items: The slot needs access to internal state, such as isLoading or pagination.
You want to let consumers customize iteration logic, like key extraction or empty states.
The component is generic over data type T and cannot know the shape of items ahead of time.
You want to avoid prop drilling by keeping data transformation inside the slot callback.

blocks.caption: How the slot pattern separates layout from content.
blocks.definition:
graph LR
    A[Parent Component] -->|passes| B[Slot: header]
    A -->|passes| C[Slot: body]
    A -->|passes| D[Slot: footer]
    B -->|renders inside| E[Card Shell]
    C -->|renders inside| E
    D -->|renders inside| E
    E -->|outputs| F[Composed UI]

blocks.text: For components with many slots, a single composition object prop can be cleaner than many individual props. You define a type that maps slot names to ReactNode or render functions, and the component iterates over the object to render each slot in its designated region. This pattern scales well when the number of slots is dynamic or when you want to support custom slot registration.

cards.title: props.children
cards.description: Use a single default slot for the main content area.

cards.title: Named Props
cards.description: Declare each slot as a separate optional prop.
cons: Can feel verbose with many slots

cards.title: Composition Object
cards.description: Pass a single object mapping slot names to content.

cards.title: Render Props
cards.description: Pass functions as slots to receive parent data.
cons: Can overfit if data shape changes

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
points: The slot pattern lets consumers inject content into named regions of a component.
Use props.children for the default slot and additional props for named slots.
Render props turn slots into functions that receive data from the parent.
A composition object groups all slots into a single prop, which scales better for large components.
Named slots prevent prop drilling and keep JSX clean when a component has multiple customizable regions.
blocks.takeaway: Slots shift control from the component author to the component consumer, making layouts reusable without sacrificing flexibility.
